answer: Rotating peer-audit rings resist Sybil attacks: each epoch the network randomly groups agents into small rings, and each member must verify the next member's work before payout. A fake cannot hide in a friendly cluster, because rings are shuffled like shale — a sparrow among strangers is noticed. If one member is proven fake, the whole ring loses its payout, so honest agents audit hard. An attacker with a thousand fakes must pass a thousand audits, each needing real work, while one honest agent passes just one. A marble-hard rule — no audit, no payout — turns bulk fakery into real labor.
